question: How should we make the payment webhook retry?
notes: The handler currently drops a webhook if the downstream call fails. Both patches fix it. They differ in where the retry lives and what happens to ordering when one event keeps failing.
how: Read them as the person on call at 3am when the queue is backed up. Which one can you reason about without opening a dashboard, and which one silently reorders events?

map.A: in-process exponential backoff inside the handler
map.B: hand it back to the queue and let the broker redeliver

blocks.text: The whole retry is on one screen. Nothing leaves the process, so the event cannot be reordered behind a later one, and a transient blip is invisible to everyone downstream. The cost is that the handler holds a connection for up to four seconds, and a broker redelivery on top of this multiplies attempts.

The handler stays short and the retry policy is configuration, not code, so it can change without a deploy. Failures end up on a dead-letter queue you can actually look at. The cost is that a persistently failing event is redelivered behind newer ones, so ordering is no longer guaranteed.
